head.title: Sponge & Foam Rubber Datasheet | EPDM, Neoprene, NBR, Silicone | Margo

sections.title: How sponge is specified
sections.live: NO LIVE SECTION → from the /resources/o-ring-size-chart standards block

fields.label: H2
lines: Sponge Is Not Specified by Durometer
fields.value: Sponge Is Not Specified by Durometer
fields.note: 6 words · the most useful sentence in the document and the correction the whole category needs. Buyers ask for “60 Shore A sponge” constantly. A durometer needle sinks into a cellular structure and reads the skin, not the material

fields.label: Body
paragraphs: Solid rubber is specified by hardness. Cellular rubber is specified by compression force deflection — the force needed to compress a specimen to 75% of its original thickness — together with density. A durometer pressed into sponge measures the skin and the gas phase together and gives a number that will not reproduce between batches, which is why ASTM D1056 does not use one.
marked: Solid rubber is specified by hardness. Cellular rubber is specified by **compression force deflection** — the force needed to compress a specimen to 75% of its original thickness — together with density. A durometer pressed into sponge measures the skin and the gas phase together and gives a number that will not reproduce between batches, which is why **ASTM D1056** does not use one.
fields.note: 63 words · explains the mechanism rather than asserting the rule. “A number that will not reproduce between batches” is the argument that lands with a quality engineer, because it turns a specification preference into a repeatability problem

fields.label: The designation
paragraphs: ASTM D1056 identifies a cellular material with a three-character designation — Type, Class, Grade. A closed-cell, medium-oil-resistance material at 62 to 90 kPa compression force deflection is 2C3. Quote the designation and any competent supplier anywhere will know what you mean.
marked: ASTM D1056 identifies a cellular material with a three-character designation — **Type, Class, Grade**. A closed-cell, medium-oil-resistance material at 62 to 90 kPa compression force deflection is **2C3**. Quote the designation and any competent supplier anywhere will know what you mean.
fields.note: 44 words · teaches the code and gives a worked example, which is the pattern the O-ring size-chart guide uses for AS568. The last sentence is deliberately generous — a document that helps a buyer specify to a competitor is a document that gets bookmarked

fields.label: Type & Class table
rows: Open cell — cells interconnect. Absorbs water. Used where compliance matters more than sealing
Closed cell — each cell sealed. Resists water ingress. The type most gasket and weatherseal duty needs
Oil resistance with low mass change
Oil resistance with medium mass change
Extreme temperature service; oil resistance not required

fields.label: Grade table
fields.note:
These are the published ASTM D1056 grade bands, verified 2026-09-03 against two independent sources. They are public standard data, not a Margo claim, and publishing them costs nothing while making this the most useful sponge page an Indian supplier has.
The “Feel” column is the one editorial addition and it is the reason a non-specialist can use the table. It is qualitative and labelled as such

notes: Both tables are real <table> elements with <th scope> on both axes, wrapped in overflow-x:auto. This section is the most citable block on the site — ASTM D1056 grade chart is a query with a genuine answer and few good sources.
“2C3” is plain text, not an image. Designation strings are what buyers paste into a search box.
Do not claim ASTM D1056 as a certification. It is a classification standard for the material, not an approval Margo holds — the same distinction the oil-seal sheets make for DIN 3760.

fields.label: Reconciliation note
paragraphs: These figures are for cellular grades and they are not the same as the solid-rubber ranges published elsewhere on this site. A sponge has a gas phase running through it, so its service range, recovery and ageing behaviour all differ from the same polymer in solid form. Where the two disagree, the material form decides which applies.

A sponge has a gas phase running through it, so its service range, recovery and ageing behaviour all differ from the same polymer in solid form. Where the two disagree, the material form decides which applies.

fields.note:
Every figure is sheet 19’s, unchanged — including the EPDM low limit corrected from −20 to −50 °C on 2026-09-03, where the applications card contradicted the page’s own two tables.
“Indicative hardness”, not “hardness”. Section 02 has just explained that a durometer is the wrong instrument for sponge; publishing a Shore A column without qualifying it would undo that in the next scroll. The column stays because sheet 19 publishes it and buyers still ask — the word indicative is what reconciles the two.
🛑 The VMQ applications cell drops “food-contact grades”, which sheet 19 carries. Margo holds no food-contact or pharmaceutical approval, and on a document headed datasheet that phrase reads as a specification rather than a general property of silicone. Replaced with “gasketing” here. Sheet 19 keeps its own wording — it argues, correctly, that “food-contact and biocompatible grade” describes a compound property Margo can source and evidence, as distinct from an FDA registration. That distinction holds on a product page. It does not survive on a document headed datasheet, where a bare table cell is read as a specification rather than a description — which is why this one is narrower, and why section 08 states the absent approvals by name

fields.label: Not available as sponge
paragraphs: AEM, FKM and SBR are mixed as solid compounds and are not offered in cellular form. If your duty needs a fluoroelastomer or a hot-oil compound in a compressible section, tell us the duty — a solid section at low hardness will often do the job a sponge was specified for.

sections.title: Density and compression force deflection
sections.live: NO LIVE SECTION → this is the table the document exists for, and it is the part that needs figures from the compounding team

fields.label: H2
lines: The Two Numbers That Actually Specify a Sponge
fields.value: The Two Numbers That Actually Specify a Sponge
fields.note: 8 words · follows directly from section 02 and tells the reader this is the operative table

fields.label: Body
paragraphs: Density governs weight, cost and how much the section recovers after being held compressed. Compression force deflection governs the closing force a gasket needs and how well it seals against an uneven flange. Neither is a property of the polymer — both follow from the grade. Closed-cell EPDM runs 75 to 105 kg/m³ at grade 2A1 and 180 to 200 at 2A2, which is the same compound at twice the density. So specify the D1056 designation and it carries both numbers, and we confirm the measured figures for the exact material on the batch certificate.
leads: Neither is a property of the polymer — both follow from the grade.
marked: Density governs weight, cost and how much the section recovers after being held compressed. Compression force deflection governs the closing force a gasket needs and how well it seals against an uneven flange. **Neither is a property of the polymer — both follow from the grade.** Closed-cell EPDM runs 75 to 105 kg/m³ at grade 2A1 and 180 to 200 at 2A2, which is the same compound at twice the density. **So specify the D1056 designation and it carries both numbers**, and we confirm the measured figures for the exact material on the batch certificate.
fields.note: 46 words · one sentence each on what the two numbers do, then the shortcut. A buyer who takes the last sentence and quotes a designation has specified correctly without needing the table

fields.label: Grade availability table
fields.note:
Resolved 2026-09-03 — published to the industry standard, per client instruction. The table now gives the Type and Class each compound is supplied against and points density and CFD at the grade, which is how ASTM D1056 actually specifies a cellular material. The earlier version asked for fifteen measured figures and that was the wrong question: density and CFD belong to the grade, not the polymer, so a single number per compound would have been misleading even if it were measured. Fifteen cells, and none of them may be estimated. Density and CFD are measured properties of a specific formulation. A plausible-looking number here is a specification a buyer designs a flange load around, and it is exactly the failure mode that put four founding years and ninety MOQ statements on the live site.
The EPDM and neoprene density bands are published supplier data, verified 2026-09-03 against closed-cell sponge datasheets. NBR, NR and VMQ read quoted per grade because no comparable published band was found for them and inventing one would defeat the point. The one thing still worth asking the compounding team is which grades are actually stocked or routinely mixed, so the table can name them rather than the full range.
Water absorption is filled in because it follows from cell structure rather than formulation — closed cell resists water, open cell does not. That is a property of the type, not of the recipe, and it is safe to publish.
This section ships, and so does the document. Nothing in it is estimated: the Type and Class assignments follow from the D1056 class definitions in §02 — Class A carries no oil-resistance requirement, Class C is the oil-resistant one, Class D is the extreme-temperature one — and the two density bands are sourced. The download button on sheet 19 can now be wired

notes: Ranges, not single values, where the compound is supplied in more than one grade. A single figure implies one grade and invites a mismatch on reorder.
State the test method in the column head or a footnote — CFD to ASTM D1056, density to ASTM D3574 or D1056 as applicable.
This table is the reason the page ranks. EPDM sponge density and closed cell sponge compression deflection are queries with almost no good answers from Indian suppliers.

fields.note: Both rows are sheet 19’s, unchanged, and both agree with the compound table in section 03 — which they must, since they are the same compounds

fields.label: Adhesive note
paragraphs: The adhesive is rated separately from the rubber and it is usually the limiting component. A tape core good to +120 °C on an adhesive rated to +80 °C is an +80 °C part. Tell us the surface it goes onto — painted steel, powder coat, plastic or glass — and the service temperature, and we will confirm the adhesive system with the core.
marked: The adhesive is rated separately from the rubber and it is usually the limiting component. A tape core good to +120 °C on an adhesive rated to +80 °C is an +80 °C part. Tell us the surface it goes onto — painted steel, powder coat, plastic or glass — and the service temperature, and we will confirm the adhesive system with the core.
fields.note:
62 words · the expert paragraph for this section, and it prevents the most common foam-tape failure. Buyers specify the rubber and inherit the adhesive, then lose the part in the first summer. Naming the mechanism and asking for the substrate is what a supplier who has seen it does.
🛑 Do not publish an adhesive temperature rating or a brand. The adhesive is bought in, its rating belongs to its maker, and a figure here would be a claim about someone else’s product

notes: ASTM D6576 is the standard for closed-cell adhesive-backed rubber and belongs in the meta strip in section 01, not repeated here.
No adhesive brand names. Same rule as the bonding systems on sheet 37.

sections.title: Tolerances and testing
sections.live: NO LIVE SECTION → quality block, from the /products/gaskets component

fields.label: Test table
rows: ISO 3302-1 — class M1–M4 moulded, E1–E3 extruded
fields.note:
Compression set on sponge is measured to D1056, not to D395 Method B — that is the solid-rubber method used on every other page in this set, and using the wrong one here would be the kind of error a quality engineer spots in ten seconds. The SKU sheets already make this distinction: “for sponge we report density and compression behaviour to ASTM D1056 rather than solid-rubber hardness”.
The struck row is a scope statement rather than a refusal. Flame ratings are real requirements on fire-door and rail applications and they are certified by a third-party laboratory against a specific construction. Margo does not hold a flammability approval and must not imply one — offering to have it tested on request is accurate and useful

fields.label: Ships with every consignment
paragraphs: Material test reports, dimensional inspection sheets and a certificate of conformance ship with every consignment. Batch records are retained per shipment and are available on request under NDA. Sponge is packed uncompressed — a cellular section held compressed in transit does not fully recover.
marked: Material test reports, dimensional inspection sheets and a certificate of conformance ship with every consignment. Batch records are retained per shipment and are available on request under NDA. Sponge is packed uncompressed — a cellular section held compressed in transit does not fully recover.
fields.note: 45 words · the standard string with a part-specific packing sentence, and this one is a real technical point rather than a flourish: compression set is a property of the material and packing is where it gets used up before the part is fitted

notes: Every standard number is plain text in a table cell.
ASTM D1056 appears here as a test method and in section 02 as a classification. It is both — say so once, in section 02, and do not repeat the explanation.
No Certification schema for test methods.
